q: Is Love Fist a real band?
a: No. Love Fist is a fictional rock band written for GTA Vice City (2002), heard on V-Rock with "Dangerous Bastard" and "Fist Fury". The GTA wiki marks both songs as made for the game.

q: Is Axl Rose really in GTA San Andreas?
a: Yes. GameSpot's 2004 soundtrack coverage lists Axl Rose as the voice of K-DST's DJ Tommy "The Nightmare" Smith. Chuck D, George Clinton and Sly and Robbie also voice San Andreas DJs.

q: What radio station is Karl Lagerfeld on in GTA IV?
a: Hypebeast reported in 2008 that Karl Lagerfeld is a GTA IV radio DJ. The GTA wiki names his station as K109 The Studio, a disco station.

q: Does the GTA IV radio news react to your missions?
a: Yes. Rockstar said in 2008 that Weazel News gives interactive bulletins through the story, and the GTA wiki lists mission-linked reports such as the McReary brothers' deaths after "Blood Brothers".

q: Why does Lazlow's character get worse in every GTA?
a: Lazlow told IGN at San Diego Comic-Con that Dan Houser deliberately made the in-game Lazlow sadder and less like him each game. In GTA V, Houser told him he would get to dance in his underwear.
Lazlow left Rockstar in 2020 and joined Dan Houser at Absurd Ventures. Asked in 2025 whether he would appear in GTA VI, he said he doubted it.

q: When did GTA get the radio wheel?
a: Per the GTA wiki, the radial radio wheel arrived with GTA V and GTA Online in 2013; earlier games used a looping next and previous selector. The 2021 Definitive Edition trilogy added a wheel to the older games.

q: Who wrote the fake radio ads in GTA?
a: GTA 2's ads were written by Michael Keillor at DMA Design. From GTA III, Dan Houser and Lazlow wrote the commercials and Lazlow produced them, per the GTA wiki and Lazlow's 2024 ShortList interview.
